why: The threshold that decides whose speech is acted on, derived from measurement rather than chosen. Kept so a later calibration on more recordings has a baseline to beat rather than starting over.

owner.note: Measured through the enrollment window's own Test my voice, one utterance each.

strangers.note: Synthetic. Nine LibriTTS speakers on two English lines each, best score per speaker, plus the Russian Piper voice. A weak proxy for a real impostor and not an impostor rate.

previous_profile.note: Recorded in one sitting at one volume. Cohesion 0.8433 — nominally the top band — and it scored 0.54 against its owner speaking quietly, under a threshold of 0.55.

chosen.reasoning: Uneven on purpose. Four measurements do not describe a voice — a morning voice, a cold, a headset instead of the onboard microphone all sit somewhere below 0.65 and none have been measured — so the owner's side gets the larger margin. A missed match asks the person to repeat themselves; a false match decides only whose speech is listened to, and every action still goes through the Policy Engine.

to_calibrate_later: Collect real utterances across conditions and set the threshold from the owner's measured low percentile rather than from four points. Real impostor recordings would replace the synthetic strangers entirely.
